clue.text: Mere copper wire’s ultimate tool for potter (4,3)

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of 'wire' is its last, E

blocks.note: a mere is a small lake or pool
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A length of copper wire at the edge of a pond turns out to be a handy tool for someone potting about.
explanation.walkthrough: A potter here is not a ceramicist but a player who pots balls on a pool table. The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool cue is the stick a player uses to pot balls.

clue.text: Bird rising aloft very loudly over home (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising turns UP upwards to read PU
in a down clue, FF sits over IN

blocks.note: ff = fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A bird climbs high into the sky, calling noisily above its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the bird itself rising; the word only flips UP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a stubby seabird with a colourful beak.

clue.text: Get rigid old ship if last in jetty (6)

indicators.note: the last letter in 'jetty' is Y

explanation.surface: An old ship tied up at the end of a jetty might stiffen and seize up.
explanation.walkthrough: SS for steamship is the common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is to turn into bone, and so to become rigid.

clue.text: Restricting way to scamming that’s heartless and rotten (6,3)

indicators.note: remove the heart, the middle letter N, from CONNING

explanation.surface: A crooked scheme is described as cold-hearted and corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a road-works phrase: 'way' is a road, restricted by laying out traffic cones.
explanation.definitionFit: Coning off a road closes or narrows it with traffic cones.

clue.text: Errant teen I reformed as performer (11)

indicators.note: the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward teenager straightens out and takes to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'reformed' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: singers, comedians and magicians who put on a show for an audience are all entertainers.

clue.text: Avoided second defender (4,4)

blocks.note: something left alone has been avoided
to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone dodged the job of backing up a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as a noun or ordinal, but it is the verb: to second = to back.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the left back plays in the back line on the left flank, whose job is stopping attacks.

clue.text: Many empty libraries to stock books (4)

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters: L and S
LS holds OT as a library holds stock

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Plenty of libraries stand empty and need books on their shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Testament is the usual crossword source for 'books' (OT or NT).
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal speech: 'lots of people came' says the same as 'many people came'.

clue.text: Element on boats ignoring core of the work regulations (7,4)

indicators.note: YACHTS leaves out a letter
the core of 'the' is its middle letter H

blocks.note: a factor is an element in a situation
middle letter of 'the', dropped from YACHTS

explanation.surface: Some element aboard the boats pays no heed to the heart of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Factory Acts were the British laws governing conditions in factories from the nineteenth century on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Factory Acts were laws regulating work in factories.

clue.text: Great performance getting round nuisance on foot, hazard to driver (5,6)

indicators.note: to get round something is to encircle it, so BLINDER wraps itself round CORN

blocks.note: to play a blinder is to give a brilliant performance
a corn is a painful patch on the foot

explanation.surface: A star turn is achieved despite a sore foot — something that could trip up a golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blinder' is British slang for an outstanding performance, as in 'he played a blinder'. The driver is a motorist, not a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind corner is a bend with no view of oncoming traffic, a danger for drivers.

clue.text: Understanding son acting badly (9)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged badly and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A parent is sympathetic about their son's poor performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' reads as a kind parent; it is the adjective meaning aware.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cognisant of something is to be aware of or understand it.

clue.text: One that’s cold consumes tonic (6)

an ace counts one in cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'One that's cold' looks like a single phrase about a chilly person; 'one' and 'that's cold' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracer is a tonic or stiff drink that braces you.

clue.text: On and off, church is means of support (8)

blocks.note: milk gone off has turned sour

explanation.surface: Someone's attachment to the church is an on-and-off source of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On and off' looks like a phrase for intermittently; the words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you can fall back on or draw from when in need, like savings or friends, is a resource.

clue.text: Nosy neighbours welcoming bird-watcher in the end (7-9)

blocks.note: a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally'; 'in' is a link and 'the end' gives CURTAINS.

clue.text: Again experience nurses ultimately desperate for support (7)

indicators.note: RELIVE holds E as a nurse holds a baby
the last letter of 'desperate'

clue.text: Hosiery items for sale among fine things around front of shop (7,9)

indicators.note: STOCK goes among the other letters

a shop's stock is its items for sale

explanation.walkthrough: 'Items for sale' sounds like the whole of the stock on show; only the shop's stock goes inside, and 'around' is the signal to rearrange, not to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: these are leg coverings woven in an open diamond mesh like a fishing net, one kind among tights and socks.

clue.text: Like court proceeding barring one of stars (6)

clue.text: Herb increased resistance within 31 days (8)

blocks.note: May is a month of 31 days

clue.text: Soldiers in buff shot (8)

to have a shot = to have a try

clue.text: Launched ball at ninepins we heard striking (4)

clue.text: Immunise number in critical care area recently (9)

clue.text: Unwelcome wrapper in garden? (8)

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by packaging litter blown into their garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapper' suggests packaging; bindweed wraps itself round other plants, and a weed is unwelcome by definition.

clue.text: See almost everyone stifled in urban neighbourhood (8)

indicators.note: ALL loses its last letter
AL is smothered inside CITY

blocks.note: ALL, everyone, without its last letter

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the district around a particular place, where people live nearby.

clue.text: Work with beer technology to lose current milky quality (11)

clue.text: Source of heat in Asian food involving new coating on noodle (8)

clue.text: Find fault about way of speaking (4)
